title: Ar-Razzaq, the Provider
hook: the Provider, of bread and of every other kind of provision

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Ghaffar: the servant who kept returning, and was forgiven again. Your line was forgiven again. When the same old thing came back, did you turn back once more? Day two hundred forty-five.

Early morning, before the traffic. Look up at the birds leaving a tree. They don't have jobs or savings accounts. They don't know where breakfast is. They just go. And in the evening, if you're watching, they come back, and somehow they've eaten. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ pointed at exactly that. Umar reports it, and Tirmidhi records it: if you relied on Allah as He truly should be relied on, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds. They go out in the morning hungry, and come back in the evening full. Notice one small word in there: they go out. Today: Ar-Razzaq, the Provider.
screen: `BIRDS LEAVING A TREE AT DAWN.` → `OUT HUNGRY, BACK FULL.` → `THEY GO OUT.`

segments.voice: Ar-Razzaq comes from the root r-z-q, and its noun, rizq, means provision: whatever sustains you. Here is Pickthall's translation from Surah adh-Dhariyat: Lo! Allah! He it is that giveth livelihood, the Lord of unbreakable might. The form razzaq, like ghaffar yesterday, means again and again, to everyone, without running out. The Qur'an says in Surah Hud that there is no creature moving on the earth whose provision isn't upon Allah, and He knows where it rests and where it's kept. The ant, the whale, the baby, the old man. Rizq is wider than bread. Scholars list many kinds: food and water, yes, but also health, knowledge, friends, a family, a job, time, a good night's sleep, and the faith in a person's heart. The bread is one door into a whole house of provision. Now back to the birds. They trust, and they fly. Muslims have always read trust in Allah, tawakkul, as including effort. Tirmidhi records a man asking whether he should tie his camel or trust in Allah. The answer: tie it, and trust. You do the work; the provision comes from somewhere you don't control. That takes a weight off. It doesn't make you lazy. It makes you less frantic. This week has been a string of names: the Holy, Peace, the Giver of Safety, the Creator, the Fashioner, the Forgiving, and now the Provider. You were made, shaped, kept safe, forgiven, and fed. That's a week's worth.
screen: `R-Z-Q — PROVISION, WHAT SUSTAINS.` · `EVERY CREATURE, EVERY DAY.` · `BREAD, HEALTH, KNOWLEDGE, FRIENDS.` · `TIE THE CAMEL, AND TRUST.` · then, large: `PROVIDED FOR.`

segments.voice: Sit, and think about the last thing you ate. Trace it back. Who cooked it, or packed it? Who drove it to the store? Who grew it, harvested it? Where did the rain come from that made it grow? Follow the chain as far as you can, one breath for each link. Then think of one other kind of provision in your life right now: a friend, a skill, a quiet hour. Hold both. If you pray, you can say alhamdulillah for them. The bell holds the time.
Ar-Razzaq. The Provider, who gives provision again and again to every creature: bread, and every other kind of rizq. Today's word.
Your line: provided for. Before your next meal, pause for one breath and give thanks, and after it, notice one thing that fed you that wasn't food. Day two hundred forty-five.

howItsDone: Muslims say bismillah before eating and alhamdulillah after, thanking Allah as the Provider; many speak of their income, family and health as rizq, and pair effort with tawakkul, trust, in the spirit of tie your camel and trust.

myth: rizq means only food and money
scholars include health, knowledge, friends, time and faith.
trusting Allah means you don't need to work
tie your camel, and trust. the birds still go out.
the Qur'an says every moving creature's provision is upon Allah

fork.setup: you arrive with your camel. should you tie it, or leave it loose and trust in Allah?
options: leave it loose: trust is enough
fork.reveal: tie it, and trust (Tirmidhi). effort and trust go together.

original.note: Arabic: the Provider, again and again; from r-z-q, provision.

trapdoor: what you thought: God gives people food.
what it means: the one who provides every creature with every kind of sustenance, again and again.
what a scholar hears: 51:58; 11:6; Tirmidhi 2344, the birds; Tirmidhi 2517, tie the camel; tawakkul includes taking means.
